subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, and should `full` be the only tier that admits `bootstrap-extra-files` hook additions?
rationale: The implementation is bounded, but choosing a new prompt/context config knob affects session-state behavior, upgrade expectations, hook extras, and overlapping bootstrap-control proposals in a way automation should not decide.

options.title: Sponsor focused tier contract
options.body: Proceed with this PR shape after documenting the setting publicly and preserving the no-override defaults plus tested hook-extra semantics.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap selection
options.body: Pause this PR and design one selector contract with the broader deterministic bootstrap/context-injection work before adding a new default knob.

options.title: Decline the config knob
options.body: Keep current fixed filters and steer users toward existing context-injection, bootstrap budget, lightweight-context, or future doctor guidance instead.

recommendation.title: Sponsor focused tier contract
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR shape after documenting the setting publicly and preserving the no-override defaults plus tested hook-extra semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The subagent bootstrap limiting history and prior review context make this the best available owner for the product/API call.
